Subject: Vanguard onboarding: dedicated GPU pool simulations & region selection

Hi Laura / Vanguard onboarding team,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Dedicated. We're kicking off the dedicated capacity planning for Vanguard's LLM feature set. To align expectations and size the initial GPU pool + burst policy, can you confirm the following by EOD Friday?

- Target peak qps (reads/writes) and percent of traffic that needs sub-250ms token latency.
- Expected daily traffic shape (steady vs spiky; any predictable batch windows).
- Any regulatory constraints requiring data residency (we've tentatively scoped us-east-1 and eu-west-1).

Attached is a starter config (vanguard_multipool_params.xlsx) with the nominal workload we used for the sims. We'll run throughput/latency simulations against two candidate regions and a three-region variant if you want APAC added.

Primary asks for Vanguard: please confirm SLO targets and whether you'd like autoscale to prefer cold-start burst (short-lived GPUs) vs pre-warmed reserved capacity. If you have specific ops windows for deployment, drop those here.

Next steps from us after confirmation:
1) Run two simulation sweeps (single-pool + multi-pool) and return sim_results_summary.pdf with recommended pool sizes and autoscale rules.
2) Draft a go-live playbook (handshake meeting + canary plan).
3) Prepare network and KMS integration checklist for your security team.

Thanks — happy to set a 30-min sync to walk through the sim outputs once we have your numbers.

Best,
Ben

Thanks Ben — forwarding to our infra and product teams. Answers inline (and copied below for clarity):

> - Target peak qps (reads/writes) and percent of traffic that needs sub-250ms token latency.

We expect peak QPS of ~1,200 inbound requests during business hours (US) with ~40% of calls requiring sub-250ms per-token latency (real-time assistant flows). Non-real-time batch workloads (embeddings + offline reranks) are ~20% of daily tokens and can tolerate >500ms.

> - Expected daily traffic shape (steady vs spiky; any predictable batch windows).

Traffic is spiky: regular daytime peaks 09:00–17:00 ET and a heavy nightly embedding batch from 02:00–04:00 ET. We may also have marketing-driven bursts (up to 2x baseline) occasionally — usually < 6 hours.

> - Any regulatory constraints requiring data residency.

Primary requirement: US-only for PII processing. EU region may be used for EU customers but not for US PII. So for MVP please prioritize us-east-1; eu-west-1 is optional for EU traffic only. APAC is low priority for now.

We are fine with you running the multi-pool sim if that helps size reserved vs burst. Attaching our network diagram and a short list of our SAML vendor notes.

Laura Simmons
Head of Platform Ops, Vanguard Cloud
laura.simmons@vanguardcloud.com

Laura / Ben — thanks for the clarification. I ran a quick pass based on the numbers Laura provided and sketched an implementation playbook below. Inlined recommendations are based on our recent Dedicated onboarding patterns.

---- Implementation playbook (high level) ----
1) Pool topology (MVP):
   - Primary: us-east-1 reserved pool sized for sustained baseline = 600 qps equivalent (recommend 8 x A100-40GB class nodes as starting point).
   - Burst: a small ephemeral burst pool (cold-startable) in us-east-1 for short marketing spikes (auto-scale policy: scale to 1.5x baseline for up to 6 hours).
   - EU: eu-west-1 separate pool for EU-only customers (defer initial capacity until after MVP; plan is 2 x A100 initially).

2) Autoscale & burst policy:
   - Primary autoscaler target: maintain 10–20ms queueing headroom for real-time flows.
   - Burst policy: allow ephemeral nodes to spin up with a 90s warm-up budget; cap cost by setting max burst proportion to 100% of baseline and max continuous burst window to 6 hours unless manually approved.
   - Lower-priority batch jobs should be routed to a separate queue with elastic compute and preemptible instances where possible.

3) Canary & rollout:
   - Canary route = 0.5% of production traffic -> 2 nodes in staging footprint (us-east-1).
   - Monitoring: token latency P50/P95, percent requests with per-token >250ms, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rate.

4) Network & security checkpoints:
   - Validate SAML flow and IP allowlist with Vanguard infra (Laura provided diagram).
   - KMS integration: roadmap item to validate envelope encryption keys prior to go-live.

5) Simulation plan & deliverables (coming from Redwood):
   - Sim sweep A: single-pool us-east-1 sizing (steady + burst window).
   - Sim sweep B: multi-pool split (us-east primary + eu-west tail) to show cost vs latency tradeoffs.
   - Deliverable: sim_results_summary.pdf + recommended pool provisioning table (we'll include cost delta estimates).

6) Ops handover checklist (short):
   - Run smoke tests (auth, inference, KV cache warm) in staging.
   - Run planned failover (region to region) and validate fallbacks.
   - Schedule 1-hr go/no-go with Vanguard ops + Redwood SRE.

Attachments I'll include after the sims: sim_results_summary.pdf with node counts, expected p99 latency and cost. For now, Ben — can you schedule the 45-min simulation review the week of July 13? Laura — does July 14 or 15 work for a handshake?

—Monica
